summary: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs a remote-controlled shell/PTY and file/exec surface driven by a WebSocket peer
details: The package's main entry establishes an outbound WebSocket connection to a configured server URL and dispatches incoming messages to handlers that: (1) spawn a local interactive shell via node-pty on `terminal_create` (PowerShell/cmd on Windows, $SHELL/bash on POSIX) and write server-supplied bytes directly into that PTY's stdin on `terminal_input` (terminal.js handleTerminalCreate/handleTerminalInput; router in connection/message-router.js); (2) expose remote file read/write, git commit/push, and arbitrary TCP port proxying to the same peer; (3) accept an `upgrade_agent` message that shells out to `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@<latest>` via a detached upgrade.sh/upgrade.bat and restarts the process under systemd/launchd/PM2 (connection/upgrade.js handleUpgradeAgent). service/linux.js modifies PATH to include `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` at install/service-setup time. The default server URL is loopback and the peer is shared-secret authenticated, so realized blast radius depends on how the operator provisions the server, but the code shape is a full remote-shell / remote-file / remote-exec agent controllable by whoever holds the WebSocket credentials.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
